newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plans to issue 20-year bonds in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plans to issue 20-year bonds in 1997.

text.p: Taiwan's Finance Minister Paul Chiu said on Monday the ministry plans to issue 20-year government bonds in 1997 to alleviate state treasury burdens.
"The ministry plans to issue 20-year government bonds to make the government's funding operations more flexible and alleviate the government treasury burdens," Chiu told a news conference.

Among the ministry's goals for 1997, Chiu said his ministry planned to revise rules to exempt international financial bonds from a securities transaction tax. The tax currently stands at 0.1 percent of the value of the transaction.

Chiu vowed to continue the ministry's drive to privatise state-run financial institutions, which have more than 50 percent of the existing market share, in a bid to upgrade their operational efficiency.

To further open the island's financial market, he said the ministry would revise the Banking Law to allow banks to issue financial bonds in 1997 and allow the establishment of the island's first credit-rating agency in mid-1997.
The government would continue to relax rules on offshore banking units, the international syndicated loans market as well as the foreign exchange and bond markets.
As of the end of October 1996 Taiwan had allowed 64 offshore banking units to operate on the island with total assets of US$35.4 billion.
